docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Track meaningful research progress without pretending that raw activity equals scientific progress.

docs.title: Progress dimensions
docs.text:
1. Intellectual movement: did a key uncertainty shrink?
  2. Method movement: did formalism, algorithm, or protocol become more precise?
  3. Evidence movement: did we add or strengthen supporting evidence?
  4. Decision movement: did we commit to or kill an important path?
  5. Delivery movement: did we produce a shareable artifact?

docs.title: Research Publish-Readiness Checklist
docs.text:
Related: Research README | Collection status dashboard | Collection priority matrix

Use this checklist before publishing or heavily updating research pages.

docs.title: A) Evidence-link integrity
docs.text:
• [ ] Every major claim has at least one direct evidence link (artifact, note, transcript, manuscript section).
  • [ ] Evidence links are live (not placeholders) and point to stable files/pages.
  • [ ] If a claim depends on meeting rationale, at least one meeting-evidence link is included.
  • [ ] If metrics are mentioned, the metric definition and context are linked.

docs.title: B) Status clarity
docs.text:
• [ ] Page marks current status clearly (planned / in progress / paused / evidence-added / complete).
  • [ ] "Next action" is concrete enough for a collaborator to execute without extra interpretation.
  • [ ] Open risks include mitigation actions, not just risk labels.
  • [ ] Status wording is consistent with the dashboard and priority matrix.

docs.title: C) No-overclaim gate
docs.text:
• [ ] Future intent is not phrased as completed output.
  • [ ] Scope boundaries are explicit where results are partial.
  • [ ] Strong verbs ("proves", "solves", "guarantees") are backed by visible evidence.
  • [ ] Unresolved questions are listed with follow-up checks.

docs.title: D) Collection-first framing
docs.text:
• [ ] Page identifies whether it is collection-level, subproject-level, or artifact-level.
  • [ ] Cross-links at top/bottom point to section index and related pages.
  • [ ] Collection/subproject role is stated in plain language.
  • [ ] Visitor can find the start page for the relevant section within one click.

docs.title: E) Readability and coherence
docs.text:
• [ ] Opening paragraph explains purpose in practical terms.
  • [ ] Tables use operational columns (status, evidence, risk, next action).
  • [ ] Acronyms are expanded or contextually explained on first mention.
  • [ ] Stale TODO fragments and draft residue are removed.

docs.title: F) Final release gate
docs.text:
• [ ] A reviewer can answer "what is done, what is pending, and why trust this?" in under 3 minutes.
  • [ ] At least one mentor/collaborator onboarding link is present.
  • [ ] No sensitive/private details are unintentionally exposed.

docs.text: Given a domain description and taxonomy vocabulary, generate game instances that satisfy requested dependence patterns, or report precisely why the request cannot be realized.

docs.title: Tool Release-Readiness Checklist
docs.text:
Related: Tool roadmap and status board | Tools ecosystem architecture | Hybrid artifacts showcase

Use this checklist before publishing or substantially revising any tool page.

docs.title: A) Problem and scope clarity
docs.text:
• [ ] Problem statement describes a concrete user workflow pain point.
  • [ ] Tool role in the broader tools collection is explicit.
  • [ ] MVP scope is bounded (in-scope and out-of-scope items listed).
  • [ ] Current status lane matches the roadmap board (Done/WIP/WaitList/Flagship Next).

docs.title: B) Technical credibility
docs.text:
• [ ] Inputs, outputs, and core transformations are explicitly described.
  • [ ] Hard dependencies (schemas, adapters, identity models, storage) are listed.
  • [ ] Failure modes and edge conditions are acknowledged with fallback behavior.
  • [ ] Any claimed integration has a linked evidence page or implementation note.

docs.title: C) Non-hype quality gate
docs.text:
• [ ] Claims are measurable and non-speculative.
  • [ ] No "autonomous" or "intelligent" claims without concrete behavior description.
  • [ ] Limits and known gaps are visible.
  • [ ] Next milestone is testable with a pass/fail condition.

docs.title: D) Practical usability signal
docs.text:
• [ ] At least one end-to-end usage scenario is included.
  • [ ] Reader can identify first action to try the tool concept.
  • [ ] If coordination with other tools is required, sequence is documented.
  • [ ] Privacy/consent expectations are stated when handling personal or communication data.

docs.title: E) Publication hygiene
docs.text:
• [ ] Top/bottom related-page cross-links are present.
  • [ ] Terminology is consistent with roadmap and architecture pages.
  • [ ] Page avoids speculative diagrams and placeholder graphics.
  • [ ] Sensitive implementation details, credentials, or private endpoints are excluded.
